notes: TBox rule edit: every synchrotron accelerates particles along a straight line. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is the definition of a synchrotron (Wikipedia's first sentence calls it a cyclic accelerator). No exceptions: a synchrotron's beam travels a fixed closed path by definition (the loop need not be a circle, so the queries say "closed loop" or "ring"). Counterfactual: a straight line is how a linear accelerator works. The derived queries name made-up synchrotrons (Varda accelerator, Helsing machine, Morrow source; names without "ring") known only by their class (inheritance, 2 hops); the third is an application, a building plan, whose options are a ring and a straight tunnel. The negation is worded "some synchrotron does not ...". The near query asks the cyclotron's spiral path: same relation, a neighbouring class, and an edit that spreads to all circular accelerators would answer "a straight line" there. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the side facts need checks.
